\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.UPath}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Undirected graph reachability language]
\lean{Complexity.UPATH}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p123-b002}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p016-b002}
\label{Complexity.UPATH}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.GraphReach, Complexity.encodePATH}
A Boolean string belongs to this language exactly when it encodes a finite graph with a
symmetric adjacency relation and two designated vertices joined by a path.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Undirected reachability encodings are path encodings]
\lean{Complexity.UPATH_subset_PATH}
\label{Complexity.UPATH_subset_PATH}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PATH, Complexity.UPATH}
\difficulty{4}
If a binary string encodes a finite undirected graph with designated vertices joined by
a path, then it is an encoding of a graph with designated vertices joined by a path,
without any symmetry requirement on the adjacency relation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Encoded path edge relation]
\lean{Complexity.inEdge}
\label{Complexity.inEdge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pathEdge}
For a Boolean sequence $x$, a natural number $n$, and vertices $u,v$ among the $n$
positions, define $u$ and $v$ to be related by an edge exactly when they satisfy the
edge predicate determined by $x$ and $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric encoded edge relation]
\lean{Complexity.SymRest}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p038-b004}
\label{Complexity.SymRest}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pathEdge}
For a Boolean string $x$ and natural number $n$, define the encoded edge relation to be
symmetric on vertices below $n$ when, for every $u,v<n$, $u$ is an edge to $v$ exactly
when $v$ is an edge to $u$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of the encoded edge relation]
\lean{Complexity.symmetric_inEdge}
\label{Complexity.symmetric_inEdge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SymRest, Complexity.inEdge}
\difficulty{1}
Let $x$ be a binary string and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for all $u,v<n$, the bit
of $x$ at position $2n+2+2(un+v)$ is true if and only if the bit at position
$2n+2+2(vn+u)$ is true, where an out-of-range position is read as false. Then the
relation on vertices $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ that holds when the bit at position
$2n+2+2(un+v)$ is true is symmetric.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[U-shaped encoding condition]
\lean{Complexity.UShape}
\label{Complexity.UShape}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DblAt, Complexity.MatRest, Complexity.PlainAt, Complexity.UnaryRest}
For a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $n,s,t$, define the U-shaped encoding
condition to hold when all of the following are satisfied: $x$ has the unary-rest
property at offset $0$ and length $n$; it has the matrix-rest property at parameters
$n,0$; $s<n$; the double encoding at offset $2n+2+2n^2+2$ represents the binary
expansion of $s$; $t<n$; and the plain encoding at offset
$2n+2+2n^2+2+2\lvert\mathrm{bits}(s)\rvert+2$ represents the binary expansion of $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of unary rest length]
\lean{Complexity.unaryRest_unique}
\label{Complexity.unaryRest_unique}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.UnaryRest}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word and let $n,n'\in\mathbb{N}$. If, for each of $n$ and
$n'$, every pair of positions $2i,2i+1$ with $0\le i$ strictly below that number
contains true, while the pair at positions $2n,2n+1$ (respectively $2n',2n'+1$) contains
false followed by true, then $n=n'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of the Doubled Encoding]
\lean{Complexity.dblAt_unique}
\label{Complexity.dblAt_unique}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DblAt, Complexity.dblAt_cons}
\difficulty{5}
For every binary word $x$ and natural number $q$, if two binary words $u$ and $u'$ both
have doubled encodings starting at position $q$ in $x$, each followed by the delimiter
$01$, then $u=u'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of a Plain Suffix]
\lean{Complexity.plainAt_unique}
\label{Complexity.plainAt_unique}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PlainAt, Complexity.plainAt_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $x,u,u'$ be finite bit strings and let $r\in\mathbb{N}$. If $u$ agrees with the
segment of $x$ beginning at position $r$ at every index below the length of $u$, and
$|x|=r+|u|$, and the same two conditions hold for $u'$, then $u=u'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of encoded shape parameters]
\lean{Complexity.ushape_unique}
\label{Complexity.ushape_unique}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Complexity.UShape, Complexity.dblAt_unique, Complexity.plainAt_unique, Complexity.unaryRest_unique}
\difficulty{3}
If a bit string has the prescribed shape for natural-number parameters $n,s,t$ and also
for $n',s',t'$, then $n=n'$, $s=s'$, and $t=t'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Shape and edges of an encoded path instance]
\lean{Complexity.ushape_of_eq}
\label{Complexity.ushape_of_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.UShape, Complexity.adjWord_getD, Complexity.encodePATH, Complexity.eq_pathRaw_iff, Complexity.inEdge, Complexity.length_adjWord, Complexity.matRest_iff, Complexity.pathEdge, Complexity.rowMajor_lt, Complexity.unaryRest_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a Boolean-valued relation on the indices
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $s,t$ be such indices. If a bit string $x$ is the nested
self-delimiting encoding of the unary string of $n$ true bits, the row-major list of
entries of $A$, and the binary expansions of $s$ and $t$, then $x$ has the prescribed
unary, matrix, and endpoint shape for $n,s,t$. Moreover, for every pair of indices
$u,v<n$, the encoded path relation holds exactly when $A(u,v)$ is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Decoding a Bit String of the Specified Shape]
\lean{Complexity.exists_eq_of_ushape}
\label{Complexity.exists_eq_of_ushape}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.UShape, Complexity.adjWord_getD, Complexity.encodePATH, Complexity.eq_pathRaw_iff, Complexity.ext_getD', Complexity.inEdge, Complexity.length_adjWord, Complexity.matRest_iff, Complexity.pathEdge, Complexity.pathRaw, Complexity.rowMajor_lt, Complexity.unaryRest_iff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a bit string and $n,s,t$ natural numbers. Suppose its first field consists of
$n$ doubled true bits followed by the delimiter $01$; its next $n^2$ paired-bit
positions have equal bits in each pair and are followed by $01$; its next field is the
binary expansion of $s$ with each bit doubled and followed by $01$; and its final field
is the binary expansion of $t$, with no trailing bits. Assume also $s<n$ and $t<n$. Then
there is a Boolean adjacency matrix $A$ on the vertices $0,\ldots,n-1$ such that $x$ is
the prescribed nested pair encoding of the unary field, the row-major list of entries of
$A$, and the binary expansions of $s,t$. Moreover, for every pair of vertices $u,v$, the
bit of $x$ at position $2n+2+2(un+v)$ is true exactly when $A(u,v)$ is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding characterization of undirected path reachability]
\lean{Complexity.mem_UPATH_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_UPATH_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SymRest, Complexity.UPATH, Complexity.UShape, Complexity.exists_eq_of_ushape, Complexity.inEdge, Complexity.ushape_of_eq}
\difficulty{5}
A binary string $x$ encodes an undirected graph with $n$ vertices and designated
vertices $s,t$ that are connected by a path if and only if there exist natural numbers
$n,s,t$ and a witness that $x$ has the following format: $n$ copies of the pair $11$,
followed by the separator $01$; then $n^2$ adjacency bits, each duplicated as $00$ or
$11$, followed by $01$; then the bits of $s$, each duplicated, followed by $01$; and
finally the ordinary binary expansion of $t$, occupying the entire remaining suffix. The
format requires $s<n$ and $t<n$; the adjacency relation encoded by the matrix must be
symmetric, and there must be a path from $s$ to $t$ using edges whose corresponding bits
in $x$ are $1$.
\end{theorem}
